In addition, there was a greater decrease in total Type IIx fiber area in the traditional group compared to the superslow group (approximately 39% vs. 28%, respectively), along with a correspondingly greater increase in total Type IIa fiber area (approximately 30% vs. 1 1%, respectively). This implies that lifting at a volitionally very slow cadence does not stimulate the highest-threshold motor units. Follow-up work from the same lab found that satellite cell content was significantly greater after traditional compared to superslow training across fiber types as well (100).
